answer: Sybil resistance here rests on stake-weighted vouching: every new agent needs several distinct established peers who lock a bond behind it, slashed if the nominee proves collusive. A fake swarm must either persuade real holders to risk capital or spread its own bond across many seats, so each extra identity dilutes the payoff while raising exposed collateral. Mass registration stops paying long before quorum, like buds on a trellis that cannot all bloom at dawn. Each epoch publishes an opal-clear audit of vouching, so honest agents prune duplicates early.
